# 🇫🇷 Influencer Specialist Case Study: Activating the French Community (Candidate Brief)

This brief is your case study for the AI-native Influencer Specialist role at Fleek. It is designed to show us how you think. Read it once end to end before you start.

> **The one thing we are testing above all else:** how natively you work with AI. We want to see your real workflow. Use Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Replit, scraping tools, whatever you naturally reach for. If cost is a barrier, tell us and we will set you up with a paid account. Do not hide the AI. Show it to us!

## What to expect

This is a take-home exercise. You will build and write, then walk us through it live in a debrief. You will send us your materials 24 hours before the session. On the day you will present for about 20 minutes and then we will dig in for about 40 minutes.

## Context: how Fleek works

Fleek is a B2B marketplace for wholesale secondhand and vintage clothing. Online resellers and vintage shop owners source graded inventory from wholesaler suppliers on our marketplace. Customers fall into two broad groups that matter a lot for this exercise:

- **Hobbyist resellers:** flipping clothes as a side hustle, often on Vinted, Depop or at markets. Lower volume, price sensitive, learning the game. Large in number.
- **Pro resellers:** running reselling as a real business. Higher volume, sourcing bundles by brand and category, live selling on Whatnot, running their own shops. Fewer in number, much higher value. Many of them think Fleek is for beginners and not for them. Changing that perception is one of our hardest problems.

Our total addressable community is roughly 20,000 hobbyist and pro resellers.

## The influencer programme

The single biggest goal of our influencer programme is new customer acquisition. Influencer is currently one of our biggest channels for new customer acquisition. The mechanic is simple: a creator shares a video about Fleek with their referral code in the video/caption as the CTA, a new reseller signs up and places a first order using that code, and we attribute that customer to the creator.

- Trust matters more than reach. Creators who genuinely resell and show their real sourcing, process and tips convert far better than big accounts as they have a loyal and trusting community. Some of our top performing partners:
  - @behindthesale / @theliveneedham / @juliacrcl
- Activation is an important health metric: a signed partner who never posts is worth nothing. We measure the programme on how many partners actually post, and how often, not on how many contracts exist.

## Why France, why now

France has one of the strongest reselling cultures in Europe. Vinted is the #1 retailer above Amazon and H&M, friperie and vintage culture is mainstream, Whatnot live selling is growing fast, and French resellers already pay for private Discord communities to access coaching advice. We have a growing French community: a handful of strong performers, and a longer tail of smaller partners.

We are on a path to build trust in this market and influencer has proven to be one of the most impactful channels to do this, the questions now is: how do we scale this?

## The scenario

It is your first month. Your first project is owning France for the influencer programme. You have a modest test budget, a long tail of dormant French partners you inherited, and a mandate to drive new customer acquisition through referral codes shared in creator videos. We want to see a real plan and the beginnings of the machine that would run it.

You will produce five things. Treat each as a section of one coherent submission.

## Part 1: Build the French shortlist (use AI to build a system to find them)

Produce a shortlist of **10 French creators** you would partner with. Aim for a deliberate mix across pro reseller audiences and hobbyist reseller audiences, and tell us why each one earns its place.

For each creator, capture at least: handle and platform, an estimate of audience size and engagement, who their audience actually is (pro resellers, hobbyists, general fashion), why they fit Fleek, and which reseller segment they help us reach.

**This is the core AI-nativeness test.** We do not want 10 names you already knew. We want to see how you use AI and tooling to discover, filter and enrich a list you could not have written from memory. In your submission, show your work:

- Which tools did you use to find candidates. Search, scraping actors, platform native discovery, an LLM with browsing, something you built.
- The actual prompts you gave. Paste them. We want to read the real prompt, including the ones that failed and what you changed.
- How you filtered signal from noise. How did you separate a real reselling audience from generic fashion reach.
- How you enriched each profile. Contact routes, recent posting cadence, whether they already mention sourcing or wholesale.
- How would you take this from 10 to 10,000 influencer leads

## Part 2: Outreach to new partners (localised and personalised)

These 10 creators have never worked with Fleek. Write the outreach.

- Show us the first touch and follow ups for at least 2 of your 10, written as if you were really sending it. These should feel personal and specific to that creator, not a mail merge. If your instinct is to write in French, do it, and give us a short note on the localisation choices you made.
- Explain how you would personalise and automate at scale. You cannot hand write and send 200 messages a week. How do you use AI to keep outreach personal while covering volume. Where does the human stay in the loop and why.
- Tell us what a new French partner needs to hear that a UK one does not. Localisation is more than translation.

## Part 3: From cold outreach to signed contract

Walk us through your recruitment thinking and the process itself.

- Map the journey from first contact to a signed, activated partner. What are the stages, what moves someone from one stage to the next, and where do most people drop off.
- How do you decide who is worth chasing and who is not. What signals tell you a creator will actually post and convert, versus sign and disappear.
- What does your pipeline look like as a system. If you were running this for the whole of Fleek, not just 10 people in France, what would you build so it does not live in your head.

## Part 4: Activating partners with personalised briefings (new and existing)

A signed partner who never posts is worth nothing. Your job is to activate the partners you recruit in Parts 1 to 3 and the existing French community you inherited. The best lever we know is a great briefing: telling each creator what to post, in their voice, based on what actually works.

- Deeply understand who you are briefing. How do you build a real picture of each influencer's profile: their content style, audience, formats, what they post about Fleek and what they never would.
- Study what has already worked. Look at past high performing content from different types of Fleek creators (pro resellers, hobbyists, live sellers, haul and sourcing content). What patterns drive conversions, and how do those patterns differ by creator type.
- Build the system. Based on that understanding, design and show the beginnings of a system that creates personalised, automated briefings for influencers: the right content angle, format and CTA for each partner, generated at a scale one person could never hand write. Show us how it works, what inputs it takes, and where the human stays in the loop.

## Part 5: Phased go-to-market plan, budget and CAC

Bring it together into phased plan for activating France. Roughly a first 30, 60 and 90 day view is a good shape, but use whatever structure you think is right.

- What happens in each phase, what is the goal of each phase, and how would you know it worked.
- How do you think about budget and CAC. The programme lives or dies on cost of acquiring a new customer through referral codes. How do you allocate a limited budget across new recruitment and re-activation, how do you decide what a creator is worth, and how do you move budget toward what is working.
- How do you get partners to post more. Activation is the whole game. What levers actually increase the number and frequency of posts without simply paying more per post.

## How did you use AI

This is not optional and it is not a footnote. Document, throughout, how AI showed up in your work.

- Which tools, for which parts. Discovery, enrichment, writing, analysis, planning.
- The prompts and workflows that worked, and the ones that did not.
- Where AI made you faster or found something you would have missed, and where it got in the way or produced confident nonsense you had to catch.
- If you built any small tool, automation or reusable prompt system, show it. Something that would still work if France was 500 creators instead of 10 is more interesting than a one off answer.

Show us, do not just tell us!

## What we are looking for

We are not marking a checklist. Broadly, a strong submission shows us:

- **AI-nativeness.** AI is woven through the work as a genuine multiplier, not bolted on at the end. Real prompts, real tools, real leverage.
- **Creativity.** Angles and ideas we would not have thought of. Especially on activation and getting partners to post.
- **Relationship and community instinct.** You understand that partners are people, that France has its own culture, and that community can scale trust in a way one to one outreach cannot.
- **Commercial judgement.** You think in CAC, conversion and budget reallocation, not vanity reach. You know the goal is new customers, not big follower counts.
